_meta.purpose: Central registry of vetted sources for the field guide, reusable across cities.
_meta.howToUse: Run `node tools/research.js "<City>" "<ST>"` to get the search plan for a new city, run those searches, rank what you find, fact-check, then record the winners here before building a page. See docs/SOURCES.md.
_meta.rankScale: 1 = primary (transcribe fully); 2 = strong corroboration; 3 = supplemental / leads only.
_meta.verified: true only if a claim from the source was checked via web search during this build.

sourceTypes.label: Local TV station numbered list
sourceTypes.why: Reported, photographed, numbered — ideal to transcribe and verify against.
sourceTypes.find: search '100 hidden gems of {city}', '{n} best {city} ...'; identify the metro's ABC/CBS/NBC/FOX affiliates first.

sourceTypes.label: Atlas Obscura city/state index
sourceTypes.why: The oddities backbone. Read the index, not individual searches.

sourceTypes.label: Roadside America state index
sourceTypes.why: Second oddity net; catches what Atlas Obscura misses.

sourceTypes.label: Alt-weekly
sourceTypes.why: Best food and nightlife coverage in most metros.
sourceTypes.find: search '{city} alt weekly' (e.g. Scene, Reader, Weekly).

sourceTypes.label: City / regional magazine
sourceTypes.why: Strong on neighbourhood dining and features.
sourceTypes.find: search '{City} Magazine best of'.

sourceTypes.label: Regional business / daily news
sourceTypes.why: Openings, closings, what's actually current.
sourceTypes.find: search '{city} business journal' / the metro daily.

sourceTypes.label: Nonprofit local newsroom
sourceTypes.why: Civic, specific, often the best replacement for a shuttered daily.
sourceTypes.find: search '{city} nonprofit news' (e.g. Matters, Signal, Documenters).

sourceTypes.label: Historical society / public history project
sourceTypes.why: Authoritative on museums, monuments, buildings.
sourceTypes.find: search '{city} historical society' and university public-history projects.

sourceTypes.label: Metro / regional parks authority
sourceTypes.why: Authoritative on parks, trails, natural landmarks.
sourceTypes.find: search '{city} metroparks'.

sourceTypes.label: Official state tourism
sourceTypes.why: Baseline vetted attractions with hours.

sourceTypes.label: Local CVB / visitors bureau
sourceTypes.why: The city's own curated list, usually current.
sourceTypes.find: search '{city} CVB' or 'visit {city}' or 'explore {county}'.

sourceTypes.label: Famous travel YouTuber / blogger coverage
sourceTypes.why: Popular, watchable corroboration; signals what draws outsiders. Rank by whether they actually covered THIS city vs. the region.
sourceTypes.find: search 'famous travel YouTuber visited {city} {state}', '{creator} {city}', '{city} walking tour youtube'.

sourceTypes.label: Local creator / walking-tour channel
sourceTypes.why: Ground-level, current footage of specific streets and sites.
sourceTypes.find: search '{city} walking tour youtube', '{city} things to do youtube channel'.

sourceTypes.label: Independent travel blog round-up
sourceTypes.why: Cross-checks the mainstream list; use to corroborate, not as the spine.
sourceTypes.find: search 'best things to do in {city} {state} travel blog {year}'.

sourceTypes.label: Crowd-ranked aggregator (Tripadvisor, U.S. News, PlanetWare)
sourceTypes.why: Continuously re-ranked by review volume; the default first stop for visitors and a reusable anchor citation for marquee institutions plus a harvest list for the long tail.
sourceTypes.find: search '"{city}" top attractions tripadvisor things to do', 'best things to do in {city} US News Travel', 'PlanetWare top-rated tourist attractions in {city}'. One stable per-city URL each.

sourceTypes.label: National guidebook (Fodor's, Frommer's, Lonely Planet, National Geographic)
sourceTypes.why: Editor-written attraction rundowns; strong for tier justification and for confirming a place belongs on a first-time itinerary.
sourceTypes.find: search 'Fodor's {city} things to do', 'Frommer's {city} top attractions', 'Lonely Planet {city} best things to do', 'National Geographic guide {city}'.

sourceTypes.label: Encyclopedic authority (Britannica, Wikipedia)
sourceTypes.why: Highest-authority statement that an institution is central to the city; Wikipedia's 'List of museums in {city}' is the best single harvesting index for the museum long tail.
sourceTypes.find: search 'Britannica {city} {state} cultural life', 'Wikipedia List of museums in {city}', 'Wikipedia Tourism in {city}'.

sourceTypes.label: University visitor / student-life page (.edu)
sourceTypes.why: Official admissions and student-life pages recommend a reusable cluster of named city attractions (and the campus itself often holds visitable sights); highest-yield source family for a college town.
sourceTypes.find: search '{university} things to do in {city} students explore the city', 'site:.edu things to do in {city} student guide off campus'. Also mine student newspapers and university blogs for numbered must-visit lists.

sourceTypes.label: Official institution / parent-org site
sourceTypes.why: The primary source for a marquee place — authoritative address, hours and claims. Cite the big institutions here, not to a generic list.
sourceTypes.find: search '{parent museum org} official site {city}', '{institution} official site .org {city}'. One org often runs several museums.

sourceTypes.label: Regional heritage / conservation body
sourceTypes.why: The definitive authority and often the only tour operator for industrial-heritage sites, nature reserves and historic houses (e.g. Rivers of Steel, Audubon, a landmarks foundation).
sourceTypes.find: search '{city} industrial heritage tours', '{region} land trust / Audubon reserve', '{city} history & landmarks foundation'.

sourceTypes.label: County / suburban tourism promotion agency
sourceTypes.why: Covers the visit-worthy places outside the core city — the suburbs and day-trip counties a city-only search misses.
sourceTypes.find: search 'visit {county} county {state}', '{county} tourism hidden gems', plus the suburban weekly papers (e.g. an 'Almanac' or 'Observer-Reporter').

sourceTypes.label: Local / community newspaper (daily or weekly)
sourceTypes.why: Original reporting on a specific place — openings, history features, hours — and the paper of record for towns a metro daily skips.
sourceTypes.find: search '{place} {town} {paper}' or '{town} newspaper'; use the county daily and the suburban weekly. A story on one seed place usually links others.

sourceTypes.label: Official city / county government site
sourceTypes.why: The authority on public parks, farmers markets, recreation and events — and on a place's official address and whether a city-run venue is currently operating. Ideal for verifying open/closed status and locations.
sourceTypes.find: search '{city}.gov' or '{city} official site parks/events/farmers markets'; prefer the .gov domain over aggregators.

sourceTypes.label: Michelin Guide — stars & Bib Gourmand
sourceTypes.why: The most rigorously fact-checked restaurant authority: anonymous inspectors, published star (1-3) and Bib Gourmand (great value) lists per city. Each listing is a verifiable, dated entry with the restaurant's address.
sourceTypes.find: guide.michelin.com/us/en/new-york-state/restaurants — filter by Bib Gourmand and by stars; record each restaurant's borough + address.

sourceTypes.label: James Beard Foundation Awards
sourceTypes.why: National, juried culinary awards (winners + nominees) — credible, dated, verifiable. Good for anchoring a city's most significant restaurants and chefs.
sourceTypes.find: search 'James Beard Award winners <city>' and the Foundation's official awards database.

sourceTypes.label: Reputable food media (Eater, The Infatuation, Bon Appétit)
sourceTypes.why: Bylined, reported restaurant journalism with standing city maps/guides. Corroborate the spine and catch what's current.
sourceTypes.find: Eater <city> 'essential' / 'best' maps; The Infatuation city guides; Bon Appétit / NYT Food.

sourceTypes.label: Film & TV location guides
sourceTypes.why: Movie/TV shooting locations and pop-culture landmarks are documented and fact-checkable by their real, visitable address (the Ghostbusters firehouse, the Friends building, the Sanctum Sanctorum exterior). Credible when the address is confirmed.
sourceTypes.find: On Location Tours, Scouting NY, Atlas Obscura film-locations, official brand flagships; confirm the real street address.

pittsburgh-pa.name: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania

findings: Full web-researched, fact-checked build on the Cleveland interactive engine — 27 sights + 17 food/markets/farms, incl. Markets (the Strip District, Neighborhood Flea) and Farms (Soergel, Trax, Simmons).

Substantial expansion (27→40 sights, 17→30 food) — the coverage was too thin for a city this size. Added Heinz History Center, Children's Museum, PNC Park + the Roberto Clemente Bridge / Three Sisters, the Fred Rogers statue, the Pittsburgh Zoo, Carnegie Library Main, Soldiers & Sailors Memorial, Allegheny Cemetery, Frick Park, East Carson St, Kentuck Knob, Idlewild & SoakZone, Meadowcroft Rockshelter. Food/markets/farms added: the Original Hot Dog Shop, Morcilla, Superior Motors, S&D Polish Deli, De Luca's, La Prima, Page Dairy Mart, Millie's, Enrico Biscotti, Wigle Whiskey, East End Brewing, Dancing Gnome — and Triple B Farms (u-pick, per user request).

Major expansion to Cleveland-parity (40→111 sights, 30→68 food; 179 places total) with two new regions — 'South Hills & the Southwest' and 'Eastern Suburbs & River Valleys' — and a full within-region re-rank.

Broadened the SOURCE LIST per user request: added crowd-ranked aggregators (Tripadvisor, U.S. News, PlanetWare), national guidebooks (Fodor's, Frommer's, Lonely Planet, National Geographic), encyclopedic authorities (Britannica, Wikipedia museums list), university visitor guides (Pitt, CMU, Duquesne, Chatham + student papers), the official institution sites (Carnegie Museums org, cmoa.org, carnegiemnh.org, pittsburghzoo.org, aviary.org), regional heritage bodies (Rivers of Steel, Audubon W. PA, PHLF, Battle of Homestead) and suburban/county outlets (Visit Washington County, Observer-Reporter, The Almanac, TribLive, PA Bucket List). Method codified in docs/SOURCES.md and tools/research.js.

RE-CITED the marquee institutions the user flagged as under-sourced: Carnegie Museum of Natural History → carnegiemnh.org + PlanetWare + Tripadvisor + Britannica; Carnegie Museum of Art → cmoa.org + U.S. News + PlanetWare; Pittsburgh Zoo → pittsburghzoo.org + U.S. News (#5) + PlanetWare; National Aviary → aviary.org + National Geographic ('hugely underrated') + PlanetWare + U.S. News.

New sights incl. Carrie Blast Furnaces, the Pump House / Battle of Homestead, Braddock Carnegie Library (the first in the US), the Pennsylvania Trolley Museum, the Andrew Carnegie Free Library & Espy Civil War Room (Carnegie), Dormont Pool, the Hollywood Theater, LeMoyne/Bradford/Woodville Whiskey-Rebellion houses, Monroeville Mall / Living Dead Museum, Heinz Memorial Chapel, Schenley Park & Plaza, the CMU campus set (Walking to the Sky, Randy Pausch Bridge, the Fence, Kraus Campo), Maxo Vanka Murals, the Clemente Museum, the West End Overlook and more. New food incl. Oakmont Bakery, Penn Mac, Wholey's, Reyna, Tessaro's, the Original Oyster House, Everyday Noodles, Chengdu Gourmet, Salem's, Sarris Candies, Mancini's, plus farms (Bedner's, Schramm, Kerber's, Janoski's, Shenot, Hozak).

Address + coordinate verification pass (now a hard rule, CLAUDE.md 4a): every one of the 179 places re-verified against a primary source and recorded in data/geocodes.json with source + date. 98 pins were meaningfully misplaced (>150m) and corrected — Janoski's 11.7km, Idlewild 7.9km, Triple B 5.8km, Monroeville Mall 2.8km; the Strip District had a systematic ~0.6mi longitude shift. Verified via Wikipedia coordinates, official sites, Google/Apple/OSM listings. geocheck PASS; 0 out-of-bounds, 0 stacked.

Closures caught and flagged (kept): Original Hot Dog Shop (Apr 2020) and Superior Motors, Braddock (2020). Address fixes incl. Duncan & Miller Glass Museum (525 Jefferson Ave, not 100 Ridge), Papa J's (2016 Smallman), Monroeville Mall (Mall Circle Dr), Sandcastle (1000 Sandcastle Dr).

youngstown-oh.name: Youngstown, Ohio

findings: Initial web-researched, fact-checked build (Google-Maps rendering).
Rebuilt on the Cleveland interactive engine (map, filters, trip builder, exports); Google-Maps version kept as youngstown-beta.html.

Expanded to 29 sights + 15 food/drink via web search: added Clarence R. Smith Mineral Museum, Jones Children's science center, Mill Creek Lily Pond / Lake Newport / Rose Garden / golf, downtown murals, and Warren's Dave Grohl Alley.
Added food & drink: Yosteria, Kravitz Delicatessen, The Federal, The Mocha House, Casa Di Canzonetta, and breweries Penguin City, Modern Methods (Warren), Birdfish (Columbiana).

Added a Markets category (cuisine MKT) as a standard part of the process — markets of any kind, strictly vetted per docs/SOURCES.md (well-reviewed, popular, visit-worthy; permanent or established-recurring; publicly accessible).

Included: The Youngstown Flea (curated monthly Market for Makers, downtown — regional draw), Rogers Community Auction & Flea Market (largest open-air market in the tri-state area, year-round Fridays), The Amish Market (permanent indoor, Thu–Sat), Northside Farmers Market (city's oldest, since 2003, flagged seasonal). Generic Boardman/Canfield seasonal markets rejected.
Sources added: Youngstown Live (Amish Market), youngstownflea.com, Rogers Flea Market.

Added a Farms category (cuisine FARM) for this agricultural region — visitable u-pick / petting / education farms only, per docs/SOURCES.md. Moved White House Fruit Farm here; added Detwiler Farm (Columbiana — petting zoo, u-pick, corn maze) and Molnar Farms (Poland), all flagged seasonal.
Sources added: WKBN 27 (local TV fall-farm guide), Northeast Ohio Family Fun.
Started data/local-media.json (central, updatable city -> local news/TV map); recorded Cleveland and Youngstown. Tap via `research.js --media <city>`.
Seed-place expansion (Mode C) from a user request to add Past Times Arcade — sourced the seed first, then reused those same outlets to widen the guide (50 -> 62 places; 29 -> 40 sights).

Past Times Arcade (Girard, Trumbull Co.) confirmed tier-1 — a ~600-machine pinball/arcade museum by Pinball Expo founder Rob Berk — sourced to WFMJ, Business Journal Daily (x3 articles), Mahoning Matters, the Tribune Chronicle, trade press RePlay Magazine, Tripadvisor, and the Mahoning County CVB.

Mining those outlets added, all fact-checked: National Packard Museum and the restored 1923 Robins Theatre (Warren), Noah's Lost Ark exotic-animal sanctuary (Berlin Center), TP Tools auto museum and Mill Creek MetroParks Farm (Canfield), the Mahoning County Courthouse art-glass rotunda (downtown), Sports World family fun center (Boardman), Hollywood Gaming racino (Austintown), the Ernie Hall Aviation Museum, the Ward-Thomas House Museum (Niles), and the 1831 Newton Falls Covered Bridge (the oldest covered bridge still in service in Ohio).

New reusable sources recorded: WFMJ, WKBN, Tribune Chronicle, RePlay Magazine, Tripadvisor, Truly Trumbull (Trumbull County CVB), Old Cars Weekly, Niles Historical Society. Held below the bar and dropped: chain arcades, Sutliff Museum, Skate Zone, the Firestone shopping district, and the now-merged Children's Museum of the Valley.

Address + coordinate verification pass (hard rule): all 62 places re-verified against a primary source and recorded in data/geocodes.json. 45 pins were meaningfully off (>150m) and corrected — Idora Park Experience 8.4km (it is at 4450 S Turner Rd, Canfield, not the defunct amusement-park site), Handel's 6.5km, TP Tools 6.4km, Mill Creek Golf 5.1km. Address fixes incl. Birdfish Brewing (140 E Park Ave, Columbiana — the old address was invalid), Noble Creature (126 E Rayen Ave), Mocha House (120 E Boardman St). geocheck PASS; 0 out-of-bounds, 0 stacked.

Genuinely South Bay: named blog post 'My 6 favorite Vietnamese restaurants in San Jose' (bayareafoodies.com), TikToks tagged Pho Ha Noi San Jose and a San Jose tsukemen spot, YouTube 'BEST Vietnamese Food in San Jose'. Organic reviewer of specific named restaurants, not an ad feed.

creators.name: Rachel Ahn (Silicon Valley Foodies) — Silicon Valley-specific restaurant reels
creators.credible: @siliconvalley.foodies (Rachel Ahn) shows ~147K IG followers; account name and reels are explicitly Silicon Valley / Santa Clara / San Jose focused. Featured in SJtoday's South Bay food-influencers roundup. Long reel back-catalog (2021-present) reviewing specific SV restaurants (e.g. 'My favorite Indian...' reel C2OSdGqRiz_). Scope is SV specifically, not generic SF.

creators.name: Joey Hernandez (JoeysWorldTour) — San Jose fast-food review YouTuber
creators.credible: Metro Silicon Valley 'YouTube's Fast Food King' feature; lives in San Jose, reviews fast food in his car. ~314K subs / 63M+ views; clips reference recognizable South Bay locations (KFC on Bascom, Wendy's on Union, McDonald's on Stevens Creek). NOTE: fast-food chains, not the ethnic sit-down restaurants on the Yelp-only list — limited attachment value for this guide, but a verified, genuinely local San Jose creator.

creators.name: Hee Jin Lee (HungryHungryHeeJin) — SF Bay + LA food/lifestyle creator, covers South Bay Korean & pho
creators.credible: @hungryhungryheejin ~124K IG followers, own site + press page, active TikTok — long track record. Named in Net Influencer's San Jose food-influencer list for Korean BBQ / pho / San Jose eats. NOTE: scope is broad (SF Bay + LA), not South-Bay-exclusive, so vet each post's location before sourcing.

creators.name: Esther Lee (San Jose Food Map) — San Jose native, casual local eats
creators.credible: Profiled in SJtoday's 'Local South Bay food influencers to follow': San Jose native, bartends at 55 South, documenting SJ food since 2020; ~66.5K followers reported (count is dated Jan 2024). Covers breakfast burritos, Korean groceries, new SJ eateries — squarely San Jose.

creators.name: Sachi (foodandsachi) — Bay Area food blogger active on San Jose cheap eats
creators.credible: @foodandsachi ~53K IG followers; bio 'BAY AREA FOOD BLOGGER'. Verifiably active in San Jose/South Bay: reels explicitly about San Jose spots (e.g. 'San Jose, you just got a new late-night spot... Rice Junky'). Covers SJ, SF and East Bay — vet post location, but real South Bay coverage.

creators.name: Jonathan Sahoo & Christopher (sjfoodies) — San Jose & Bay Area eats
creators.credible: @sjfoodies (Jonathan & Christopher), ~19K IG followers, bio 'Eating our way through the best food in San Jose & the Bay Area.' Named in SJtoday's South Bay influencer roundup (Jonathan Sahoo) for boba, birria and lesser-known cuisines. San Jose-centered.

creators.name: Vicky Phu (phuoodwithvicks) — San Jose Asian-cuisine foodie
creators.credible: @phuoodwithvicks, ~7.7K IG followers with a deep 848-post track record (not a burner). Named in Net Influencer's San Jose food-influencer list; covers Asian cuisines, Salvadoran and American food from the San Jose area plus homemade recipes. Modest following but genuinely San Jose-specific and organic.

creators.name: Vy (vyeatsfood_) — San Jose foodie, POV restaurant reels
creators.credible: @vyeatsfood_ 'Vy | San Jose Foodie', ~5.5K IG followers, San Jose-based, reels of specific SJ spots (banh mi, Kai Japanese Sushi San Jose, AYCE hot pot). Small but real and consistently South Bay; listed in Social Cat's San Jose creators. Lowest following on this list — weight accordingly.

creators.credible: Cincinnati Magazine profile ('Dione Wu Cooks Up Aesthetically Pleasing Food Photos'); ranked #5 among Cincinnati food & drink Instagram influencers (infludata, Mar 2026). Miami University grad based in Cincinnati.

creators.name: Cincinnati Food Blog (@cincinnatifoodies) — Cincinnati food & drink content creators

Kept as a genuinely authoritative weird-history creator rather than a large-following one.

creators.name: Julie Niesen — 'Wine Me, Dine Me' / WVXU 'Bits & Bites'; veteran Cincinnati food writer

creators.credible: Covered Cincinnati food since 2007–08; her 'Wine Me, Dine Me' blog was cited by The Washington Post, USA Today, Serious Eats, the Cincinnati Enquirer and CityBeat; now writes 'Bits & Bites' for Cincinnati Public Radio (WVXU). Longtime Over-the-Rhine resident.
